name: Green Anole
habitat: Southeastern United States, found in trees, shrubs, and buildings
funFact: Green anoles can change color from bright green to brown based on mood, temperature, or social signals.
description: The green anole is a small arboreal lizard native to the southeastern United States. Often called the American chameleon, it can shift its skin color between green and brown. Males display a pinkish-red dewlap under their throat during courtship or territorial displays.

name: Komodo Dragon
habitat: Indonesian islands, dry savanna, tropical forest edges
funFact: Komodo dragons have venom glands that deliver toxins preventing blood clotting in their prey.
description: The Komodo dragon is the largest living lizard in the world, found on a few Indonesian islands. It is an apex predator capable of taking down deer, pigs, and even water buffalo. Young Komodo dragons spend their first years in trees to avoid predation by adults.

name: King Cobra
habitat: Tropical forests of South and Southeast Asia
funFact: The king cobra is the only snake that builds nests for its eggs, guarding them fiercely until they hatch.
description: The king cobra is the world's longest venomous snake, capable of reaching lengths over 13 feet. Found in the tropical forests of South and Southeast Asia, it primarily feeds on other snakes. Its venom is potent enough to kill an elephant.

name: Green Sea Turtle
habitat: Tropical and subtropical oceans worldwide
funFact: Green sea turtles get their name from the green color of their body fat, which comes from their algae-rich diet.
description: Green sea turtles are among the largest sea turtles in the world and the only herbivorous marine turtle species. They migrate long distances between feeding grounds and nesting beaches, returning to the same beach where they were born.

name: Saltwater Crocodile
habitat: Coastal and riverine habitats in Southeast Asia and Australia
funFact: Saltwater crocodiles have the strongest bite force of any living animal, estimated at over 3700 psi.
description: The saltwater crocodile is the largest living reptile and has the strongest bite force ever measured. Found in coastal regions from eastern India to Australia, it is an opportunistic apex predator. Adults can survive in both saltwater and freshwater environments.

name: Reticulated Python
habitat: Rainforests, grasslands, and rivers of Southeast Asia
funFact: The reticulated python is the longest snake in the world, with some individuals exceeding 23 feet.
description: The reticulated python is a non-venomous constrictor and the longest snake in the world. Native to Southeast Asia, it is found in rainforests, rivers, and even near human settlements. It kills prey by constriction and can swallow animals much larger than its head.

name: Panther Chameleon
habitat: Tropical rainforests of Madagascar
funFact: Chameleons change color primarily for communication and temperature regulation, not camouflage.
description: The panther chameleon is a vibrant species native to Madagascar's tropical rainforests. Males display vivid colors ranging from blue, green, and yellow to red. They use their long, sticky tongues to catch insects with remarkable accuracy.

name: American Alligator
habitat: Freshwater wetlands, swamps, and marshes of the southeastern United States
funFact: American alligators can regulate their body temperature by opening their mouths to cool down, known as gaping.
description: The American alligator is a large crocodilian native to the southeastern United States. Once endangered, it has made a remarkable recovery through conservation efforts. It inhabits freshwater environments and is an opportunistic predator of fish, birds, and mammals.

name: Leopard Gecko
habitat: Rocky, dry grasslands and deserts of South Asia
funFact: Leopard geckos can store fat in their tails, which can detach if grabbed by a predator and later regrow.
description: The leopard gecko is a small, nocturnal lizard native to the rocky deserts and grasslands of South Asia. Unlike many geckos, it has movable eyelids and can blink. It is one of the most popular pet reptiles due to its docile temperament.

name: Eastern Diamondback Rattlesnake
habitat: Southeastern United States, coastal scrub, pine flatwoods
funFact: The eastern diamondback rattlesnake's rattle can vibrate up to 50 times per second as a warning signal.
description: The eastern diamondback rattlesnake is the largest venomous snake in North America. Found in the coastal scrublands and pine flatwoods of the southeastern United States, it uses its diamond-shaped dorsal pattern as camouflage. Its rattle serves as an auditory warning to potential threats.

name: Gila Monster
habitat: Sonoran, Mojave, and Chihuahuan Deserts of the southwestern United States
funFact: The Gila monster's venom contains a compound used in a drug to treat type 2 diabetes.
description: The Gila monster is one of only a few venomous lizards in the world, native to the deserts of the southwestern United States and northwestern Mexico. It has a stout body with bead-like scales in black and pink, orange, or yellow patterns. It spends most of its life underground.

name: Leatherback Sea Turtle
habitat: Open oceans of tropical and temperate waters worldwide
funFact: Leatherback sea turtles are the largest turtles in the world and have existed for over 100 million years.
description: The leatherback sea turtle is the largest living turtle and the fourth heaviest reptile. Unlike other sea turtles, it has a flexible, leathery carapace instead of a hard shell. It dives to depths exceeding 3,000 feet and feeds almost exclusively on jellyfish.

name: Boomslang
habitat: Savannas and woodlands of sub-Saharan Africa
funFact: Boomslang venom prevents blood clotting, causing victims to bleed from every orifice.
description: The boomslang is a highly venomous rear-fanged snake native to sub-Saharan Africa. Males are typically bright green while females are brown. It is arboreal, spending most of its time in trees, and feeds on birds, chameleons, and small mammals.

name: Green Iguana
habitat: Tropical rainforests near water in Central and South America
funFact: Green iguanas can fall from heights of 40-50 feet and survive by slowing their descent with their tail.
description: The green iguana is a large, arboreal herbivorous lizard native to Central and South America. It is excellent at swimming and can hold its breath for up to 30 minutes. Juveniles are bright green while adults may turn orange or dull grey.

name: Indian Cobra
habitat: Forests, farmlands, and urban areas across the Indian subcontinent
funFact: The Indian cobra's iconic hood markings are thought to resemble eyes, deterring predators from attacking from behind.
description: The Indian cobra is one of the 'big four' venomous snakes responsible for the most snakebite deaths in India. It is iconic for its hood, which it displays when threatened. It is found across the Indian subcontinent in a variety of habitats.

name: Rhinoceros Iguana
habitat: Dry, rocky hillsides and scrublands of Hispaniola
funFact: Rhinoceros iguanas get their name from the horn-like scales on their snouts, which resemble rhinoceros horns.
description: The rhinoceros iguana is a large, heavy-bodied lizard endemic to the Caribbean island of Hispaniola. It is named for the bony, horn-like outgrowths on its snout. It inhabits dry, rocky areas and feeds on leaves, flowers, and fruit.

name: Emerald Tree Boa
habitat: Tropical rainforests of South America, arboreal
funFact: Emerald tree boas have heat-sensing pits along their lips to detect warm-blooded prey in the dark.
description: The emerald tree boa is a bright green, non-venomous constrictor native to the rainforests of South America. It spends almost its entire life coiled on branches, waiting to ambush birds and small mammals. Its white markings along the spine help break up its silhouette.

name: Gharial
habitat: Deep, fast-flowing rivers of the Indian subcontinent
funFact: Gharials have the longest and thinnest snouts of any crocodilian, perfectly shaped for catching fish.
description: The gharial is a critically endangered crocodilian with a distinctive long, thin snout adapted for catching fish. Once found across the Indian subcontinent, it is now restricted to a few rivers in India and Nepal. It is one of the largest crocodilian species.

name: Boa Constrictor
habitat: Tropical rainforests, grasslands, and plantations of Central and South America
funFact: Boa constrictors give live birth rather than laying eggs, with litters sometimes exceeding 60 babies.
description: The boa constrictor is a large, non-venomous constrictor found throughout Central and South America. It is a highly adaptable species found in rainforests, savannas, and even near human habitations. It kills prey by constriction and is a popular species in captivity.

name: Mexican Beaded Lizard
habitat: Dry thorn scrub and deciduous forests of Mexico and Guatemala
funFact: The Mexican beaded lizard is one of only a few venomous lizards and can deliver a painful, though rarely fatal, bite.
description: The Mexican beaded lizard is a large, venomous lizard found in the dry forests and thorn scrub of Mexico and Guatemala. It has black skin with yellow or pinkish banding and bead-like scales. It is nocturnal and spends most of its time in burrows.

name: Desert Tortoise
habitat: Mojave and Sonoran Deserts of the southwestern United States
funFact: Desert tortoises can store over a liter of water in their bladders and reabsorb it during droughts.
description: The desert tortoise is a species of tortoise native to the Mojave and Sonoran Deserts. It spends up to 95% of its life underground in burrows that can be over 30 feet long. It is well adapted to extreme heat and arid conditions.

name: Black Mamba
habitat: Savannas, woodlands, and rocky outcrops of eastern and southern Africa
funFact: Despite its name, the black mamba is not black but olive-grey; the name refers to its dark blue-black mouth interior.
description: The black mamba is the fastest snake in the world and one of the most venomous. Found in eastern and southern Africa, it can reach speeds of 12 mph and strike with incredible accuracy. Its venom is neurotoxic and can be fatal without antivenom.

name: Tokay Gecko
habitat: Tropical and subtropical forests and buildings of Southeast Asia
funFact: Tokay geckos can produce one of the loudest calls of any gecko, heard up to a mile away.
description: The tokay gecko is a large gecko native to Southeast Asia, known for its loud, distinctive call. Males are territorial and aggressive, often found on walls and ceilings of buildings. It is widely used in traditional medicine in some Asian cultures.

name: Eastern King Snake
habitat: Forests, swamps, and agricultural areas of the eastern United States
funFact: King snakes are called 'kings' because they regularly eat other snakes, including venomous rattlesnakes.
description: The eastern king snake is a powerful, non-venomous constrictor found across the eastern United States. It has a distinctive chain-link pattern of white or yellow bands on a dark background. It is immune to the venom of many pit vipers.

name: Blue-Tongued Skink
habitat: Forests, grasslands, and suburban areas of Australia and New Guinea
funFact: Blue-tongued skinks flash their bright blue tongues to startle predators into backing away.
description: The blue-tongued skink is a group of lizards native to Australia, Tasmania, and New Guinea. They are known for their distinctive blue tongues, which they display as a defense mechanism. They are omnivorous, eating insects, snails, and vegetation.

name: American Crocodile
habitat: Coastal rivers, brackish lagoons, and mangrove swamps of the Americas
funFact: American crocodiles are more tolerant of saltwater than alligators, which is why they are found in coastal habitats.
description: The American crocodile is found in the coastal regions of the Americas, from southern Florida to northern South America. It is less aggressive than the saltwater crocodile and prefers brackish and saltwater habitats. It is lighter in color than most crocodiles.

name: Asian Water Monitor
habitat: Rivers, canals, mangroves, and wetlands of Southeast Asia
funFact: Asian water monitors are excellent swimmers and can hold their breath for up to 30 minutes.
description: The Asian water monitor is a large lizard native to Southeast Asia, commonly found near water. It is an opportunistic carnivore feeding on fish, frogs, birds, and carrion. It is one of the most common monitor lizards in the world.

name: Eastern Hognose Snake
habitat: Sandy, well-drained soils of eastern North America
funFact: Hognose snakes are famous for playing dead when threatened, rolling onto their backs with their mouths open.
description: The eastern hognose snake is a non-venomous colubrid found across eastern North America. It has an upturned snout used for burrowing. When threatened, it may flatten its neck like a cobra or play dead with theatrical drama.

name: Sailfin Lizard
habitat: Rivers and streams in the Philippines and Indonesia
funFact: Sailfin lizards can run across the surface of water for short distances using their flattened, fringed toes.
description: The sailfin lizard is a semi-aquatic agamid lizard found in the Philippines and Indonesia. Males have large dorsal crests that resemble sails. They are often found near water and can run bipedally across water surfaces when startled.

name: Texas Rat Snake
habitat: Forests, farmlands, and suburban areas across Texas and surrounding states
funFact: Texas rat snakes are excellent climbers and have been found in trees more than 40 feet high.
description: The Texas rat snake is a large, non-venomous colubrid native to Texas and the south-central United States. It is a powerful constrictor that feeds primarily on rodents. It is highly adaptable and found in a wide range of habitats.

name: Gopher Tortoise
habitat: Sandy, well-drained uplands of the southeastern United States
funFact: Gopher tortoise burrows can be over 40 feet long and provide shelter for more than 350 other species.
description: The gopher tortoise is a keystone species of the southeastern United States, known for digging extensive burrows. These burrows provide critical shelter for over 350 other species, including the eastern indigo snake. It is a slow-moving herbivore.

name: Bush Viper
habitat: Tropical rainforests and swamps of equatorial Africa
funFact: Bush vipers have keeled, leaf-like scales that give them a spiky, dragon-like appearance unique among snakes.
description: The bush viper is a venomous, arboreal viper found in the tropical rainforests of equatorial Africa. It has distinctive leaf-shaped, keeled scales in various colors. It is nocturnal and uses its prehensile tail to hang from branches while hunting.

name: Pancake Tortoise
habitat: Rocky outcrops and savannas of eastern and central Africa
funFact: Pancake tortoises have flat, flexible shells that allow them to wedge themselves into rock crevices to escape predators.
description: The pancake tortoise is a critically endangered species with a uniquely flat, flexible shell. Found in the rocky outcrops of East Africa, it wedges itself into crevices when threatened. It is one of the fastest tortoise species relative to its size.

name: Cottonmouth
habitat: Wetlands, swamps, and marshes of the southeastern United States
funFact: Cottonmouths get their name from the white, cotton-like lining of their mouth, which they display as a warning.
description: The cottonmouth, or water moccasin, is a venomous pit viper found in the wetlands of the southeastern United States. It is the only venomous water snake in North America. It is often found swimming with its head above water.

name: Green Basilisk
habitat: Tropical rainforests near streams in Central America
funFact: The green basilisk is also called the Jesus Christ lizard because it can run across the surface of water.
description: The green basilisk is a striking lizard found in the tropical rainforests of Central America. Males have impressive crests on their heads, backs, and tails. It is famous for its ability to run bipedally across water surfaces for short distances.

name: Cuban Crocodile
habitat: Freshwater swamps and marshes of western Cuba
funFact: Cuban crocodiles are the most terrestrial of the New World crocodiles and can gallop like a horse.
description: The Cuban crocodile is a critically endangered species found only in the Zapata Swamp and Isle of Youth in Cuba. It is highly aggressive and more terrestrial than other crocodiles. It can gallop on land and is known for its distinctive horned ridges.

name: Central Bearded Dragon
habitat: Arid woodlands, shrublands, and deserts of central Australia
funFact: Bearded dragons puff out their spiny throat scales and open their mouths to appear larger when threatened.
description: The central bearded dragon is a popular pet lizard native to the arid regions of central Australia. It displays a darkened beard when threatened or during social interactions. It basks on rocks and branches, absorbing heat to regulate its body temperature.

name: Yellow-Bellied Slider
habitat: Ponds, lakes, and slow-moving rivers of the southeastern United States
funFact: Yellow-bellied sliders can bask on logs for hours, using the sun to regulate their body temperature and digest food.
description: The yellow-bellied slider is a semi-aquatic turtle native to the southeastern United States. It has a dark shell with yellow stripes and a distinctive yellow patch on its plastron. It is one of the most common turtle species in pet trade.

name: Western Diamondback Rattlesnake
habitat: Deserts, rocky hillsides, and grasslands of western North America
funFact: Western diamondback rattlesnakes add a new segment to their rattle each time they shed their skin.
description: The western diamondback rattlesnake is one of the most dangerous snakes in North America. Found across the southwestern United States and Mexico, it is responsible for the majority of snakebite fatalities in the region. Its rattle serves as a warning when threatened.

name: Caiman Lizard
habitat: Swamps, rivers, and wetlands of South America
funFact: Caiman lizards have powerful jaws and thick, armored scales that resemble those of caiman crocodilians.
description: The caiman lizard is a semi-aquatic lizard found in the swamps and rivers of South America. It has a flattened tail for swimming and powerful jaws for crushing snail shells. Its skin resembles that of a caiman, hence its name.

name: Nile Crocodile
habitat: Rivers, lakes, and marshes throughout sub-Saharan Africa
funFact: Nile crocodiles are considered the most dangerous crocodile species to humans, with an estimated 1000 attacks per year.
description: The Nile crocodile is one of the largest crocodilian species and is considered the most dangerous to humans. Found throughout sub-Saharan Africa, it is an apex predator of rivers and lakes. It can go months without eating and has the most powerful bite of any living animal.

name: Carpet Python
habitat: Rainforests, woodlands, and rocky areas of Australia and New Guinea
funFact: Carpet pythons are nocturnal hunters that use heat-sensing pits to detect warm-blooded prey in total darkness.
description: The carpet python is a large, non-venomous snake found across Australia and New Guinea. It has a variable pattern of dark bands on a lighter background. It is arboreal and commonly found in trees and on the roofs of houses.

name: Brown Basilisk
habitat: Tropical rainforests near water in Central America
funFact: Brown basilisks can run across water using their long toes and fringed scales, earning them the nickname 'Jesus Christ lizard'.
description: The brown basilisk is a large lizard found in the tropical rainforests of Central America. It has a distinctive crest on its head and can run bipedally across water. It is semi-arboreal and often found near streams and rivers.

name: Dumeril's Boa
habitat: Dry forests and scrublands of Madagascar
funFact: Dumeril's boa can reduce its metabolic rate to survive extended periods without food, going months between meals.
description: Dumeril's boa is a heavy-bodied, non-venomous snake endemic to Madagascar. It has a tan and brown pattern that provides excellent camouflage on the forest floor. It is a ground-dwelling ambush predator feeding on mammals and birds.

name: African Spurred Tortoise
habitat: Arid grasslands and savannas of the Sahel region of Africa
funFact: Sulcata tortoises dig extensive burrows up to 10 feet deep to escape the extreme heat of the African savanna.
description: The African spurred tortoise is the third-largest tortoise species in the world, native to the Sahel region of Africa. It is named for the large, pointed spurs on its legs. It digs deep burrows to escape desert temperatures.

name: Common Caiman
habitat: Freshwater rivers, lakes, and wetlands of Central and South America
funFact: Common caimans have a bony ridge between their eyes that acts like a built-in pair of sunglasses in bright sunlight.
description: The common caiman is a medium-sized crocodilian found throughout Central and South America. It is one of the most widespread crocodilian species. It feeds primarily on fish and invertebrates and is often found in large groups basking on riverbanks.

name: Western Hognose Snake
habitat: Sandy prairies and grasslands of central North America
funFact: Western hognose snakes flatten their heads and hiss loudly when threatened, but their bluff rarely escalates to biting.
description: The western hognose snake is a small, non-venomous snake with an upturned snout used for burrowing. Found in the sandy prairies of central North America, it is known for its dramatic threat display. It feeds primarily on toads and small rodents.

name: Forest Cobra
habitat: Tropical forests and savannas of central and western Africa
funFact: The forest cobra is the largest true cobra species and an excellent swimmer, often found near water.
description: The forest cobra is the largest cobra species, found in the tropical forests and savannas of central and western Africa. It is highly venomous and can spit venom accurately. It is a strong swimmer and often found near bodies of water.

name: Veiled Chameleon
habitat: Wadis and mountainous regions of Yemen and Saudi Arabia
funFact: Male veiled chameleons have a tall casque on their heads that may help channel dew drops into their mouths.
description: The veiled chameleon is one of the most popular pet chameleon species, native to Yemen and Saudi Arabia. Males have a distinctive tall casque on their heads. It is an arboreal species that feeds on insects by projecting its long, sticky tongue.

name: Common Snapping Turtle
habitat: Ponds, lakes, and slow-moving rivers of eastern North America
funFact: Common snapping turtles can extend their necks nearly the length of their shell to strike at prey or threats.
description: The common snapping turtle is a large, freshwater turtle found across eastern North America. It has a powerful beak-like jaw and a long, prehistoric-looking tail. Unlike most turtles, it cannot fully retract into its shell, making it more aggressive on land.

name: Rough-Scaled Sand Boa
habitat: Arid deserts and sandy regions of South Asia
funFact: Sand boas spend most of their lives buried underground, with only their eyes and snout visible above the sand.
description: The rough-scaled sand boa is a small, non-venomous constrictor found in the arid deserts of South Asia. It has a stout body adapted for burrowing and spends most of its time beneath the sand. It feeds primarily on rodents and small lizards.

name: Philippine Crocodile
habitat: Freshwater rivers, lakes, and marshes of the Philippines
funFact: The Philippine crocodile is the most endangered crocodilian in the world, with fewer than 100 left in the wild.
description: The Philippine crocodile is a critically endangered species endemic to the Philippines. It is the most endangered crocodilian in the world, with a wild population estimated at fewer than 100 individuals. It inhabits freshwater rivers, lakes, and marshes.

name: Rainbow Boa
habitat: Tropical rainforests of South America
funFact: Rainbow boas have iridescent scales that refract light, creating a stunning rainbow shimmer in the sun.
description: The rainbow boa is a non-venomous constrictor found in the rainforests of South America. Its name comes from the iridescent sheen of its scales, which refract light to create a rainbow effect. It is a terrestrial species found on the forest floor.

name: Giant Plated Lizard
habitat: Rocky outcrops and savannas of southern and eastern Africa
funFact: Giant plated lizards wedge themselves into rock crevices and inflate their bodies, making them nearly impossible to extract.
description: The giant plated lizard is a large, robust lizard found in the rocky outcrops of southern and eastern Africa. It has heavy, plate-like scales and a powerful tail. It is semi-arboreal and feeds on insects, small vertebrates, and fruit.

name: Alligator Snapping Turtle
habitat: Rivers, lakes, and canals of the southeastern United States
funFact: Alligator snapping turtles have a worm-like appendage on their tongue that lures fish directly into their mouths.
description: The alligator snapping turtle is the largest freshwater turtle in North America. It has a massive head, a hooked beak, and a shell with three prominent ridges. It is an ambush predator that lies motionless on the river bottom with its mouth open.

name: Black Spiny-Tailed Iguana
habitat: Rocky areas, cliffs, and walls of Central America
funFact: The black spiny-tailed iguana is the fastest lizard in the world, capable of running at 21 mph.
description: The black spiny-tailed iguana is the fastest lizard in the world, reaching speeds of 21 mph. Native to Central America, it is found on rocky cliffs, walls, and in urban areas. It is an omnivorous species that feeds on plants and small animals.

name: Burmese Python
habitat: Tropical grasslands, marshes, and forests of Southeast Asia
funFact: Burmese pythons are one of the largest snake species and have become a destructive invasive species in the Florida Everglades.
description: The Burmese python is one of the five largest snakes in the world, native to Southeast Asia. It is a popular pet species but has become a significant invasive species in the Florida Everglades. It is a powerful constrictor that feeds on mammals and birds.

name: Ornate Box Turtle
habitat: Prairies, meadows, and grasslands of the central United States
funFact: Ornate box turtles can completely seal their hinged plastron shut, trapping themselves inside their shell for protection.
description: The ornate box turtle is a small, terrestrial turtle native to the prairies of central North America. It has a domed shell with intricate yellow and orange patterns. It can fully close its hinged plastron to protect itself from predators.

name: Common House Gecko
habitat: Human dwellings, urban areas, and tropical regions worldwide
funFact: Common house geckos are one of the most widespread lizard species on Earth, found on every continent except Antarctica.
description: The common house gecko is a small, nocturnal lizard found throughout the tropical and subtropical regions of the world. It is commonly seen on walls and ceilings of buildings, hunting insects. Its toe pads allow it to climb smooth vertical surfaces.

name: Sidewinder Rattlesnake
habitat: Sandy deserts and alkali flats of the southwestern United States
funFact: Sidewinders move using a unique S-shaped locomotion that minimizes contact with hot desert sand.
description: The sidewinder rattlesnake is a venomous pit viper adapted to desert life in the southwestern United States. It uses a distinctive sidewinding locomotion that leaves J-shaped tracks in the sand. It buries itself in sand to ambush prey and escape heat.

name: Chinese Water Dragon
habitat: Tropical and subtropical forests near water in southeastern China
funFact: Chinese water dragons can drop from heights of 40 feet and land safely on branches below.
description: The Chinese water dragon is an arboreal agamid lizard found near streams in the forests of southeastern China. Males display vibrant green with white and orange markings. It is an excellent swimmer and can hold its breath for up to an hour.

name: West African Dwarf Crocodile
habitat: Swamps, rivers, and flooded forests of western and central Africa
funFact: West African dwarf crocodiles are the most terrestrial of all crocodilians and dig deep burrows to rest in during the day.
description: The West African dwarf crocodile is the smallest living crocodile species, found in the swamps and rivers of western and central Africa. It is nocturnal and highly terrestrial, digging burrows for shelter. It feeds primarily on fish, crustaceans, and insects.

name: Cape Cobra
habitat: Semi-arid shrublands and fynbos of southern Africa
funFact: Cape cobras are highly venomous and are responsible for the most snakebite deaths in southern Africa.
description: The Cape cobra is one of the most dangerous cobras in Africa, found in the shrublands and fynbos of southern Africa. It is highly venomous with potent neurotoxin. It is a diurnal species and an excellent climber.

name: Crested Iguana
habitat: Dry forests and thorn scrub of western Madagascar
funFact: Crested iguanas can change color from green to black based on temperature and social context.
description: The crested iguana is a critically endangered species endemic to the dry forests of western Madagascar. It has a distinctive high dorsal crest and is one of the rarest iguanas in the world. It is primarily herbivorous, feeding on leaves and fruit.

name: Argentine Black and White Tegu
habitat: Grasslands, savannas, and forests of South America
funFact: Argentine tegus can regulate their body temperature during the reproductive season without relying solely on external heat.
description: The Argentine black and white tegu is a large, omnivorous lizard native to South America. It has distinctive black and white banding and a robust body. It feeds on a wide variety of foods including insects, small animals, fruit, and eggs.

name: King Brown Snake
habitat: Woodlands, forests, and grasslands of Australia
funFact: The king brown snake is technically a black snake, not a brown snake, and is in the genus Pseudechis.
description: The king brown snake, also known as the mulga snake, is one of Australia's most widespread and dangerous snakes. Despite its name, it belongs to the black snake genus Pseudechis. It is responsible for more snakebite deaths in Australia than any other species.

name: False Gharial
habitat: Freshwater rivers and swamps of Southeast Asia
funFact: The false gharial has a narrow snout similar to the true gharial but is not closely related to it.
description: The false gharial is a critically endangered crocodilian found in the rivers and swamps of Southeast Asia. It has a distinctive long, narrow snout and is one of the largest crocodilian species. It is a specialist fish-eater with a unique jaw structure.

name: Indian Star Tortoise
habitat: Dry scrublands and grasslands of India and Sri Lanka
funFact: Indian star tortoises have star-shaped patterns on their shells that help with camouflage and thermoregulation.
description: The Indian star tortoise is a small to medium-sized tortoise native to India and Sri Lanka. It has distinctive star-shaped patterns on its carapace that radiate from the center of each scute. It is a popular species in the illegal pet trade.

name: Green Anaconda
habitat: Swamps, marshes, and slow-moving rivers of South America
funFact: The green anaconda is the heaviest snake in the world, with some individuals weighing over 220 pounds.
description: The green anaconda is the heaviest and one of the longest snakes in the world, found in the swamps and rivers of South America. It is a non-venomous constrictor that feeds on deer, capybaras, and even jaguars. It spends most of its time in water.

name: Tuatara
habitat: Offshore islands and forested areas of New Zealand
funFact: Tuatara are the last surviving members of an order of reptiles that lived alongside dinosaurs over 200 million years ago.
description: The tuatara is a reptile endemic to New Zealand and the only surviving member of the order Rhynchocephalia. Often called a living fossil, it has remained virtually unchanged for 200 million years. It has a third eye on top of its head that detects light changes.

name: Eastern Water Dragon
habitat: Rivers, creeks, and wetlands of eastern Australia
funFact: Eastern water dragons can swim underwater for up to 90 minutes, closing a special membrane to keep water out of their eyes.
description: The eastern water dragon is a large agamid lizard found along rivers and creeks in eastern Australia. Males have a distinctive red chest and a spiny crest along their back. It is semi-aquatic and an excellent swimmer.

name: Spider Tortoise
habitat: Dry spiny forests of southern Madagascar
funFact: Spider tortoises are named for the radiating yellow lines on their shells that resemble a spider's web.
description: The spider tortoise is a critically endangered species endemic to the dry spiny forests of southern Madagascar. It has distinctive yellow radiating patterns on its dark shell that resemble a spider's web. It is one of the smallest tortoise species in the world.

name: Russian Tortoise
habitat: Arid grasslands and steppes of Central Asia
funFact: Russian tortoises can survive extreme temperatures by brumating underground for up to 6 months during harsh winters.
description: The Russian tortoise is a small species native to the arid steppes of Central Asia. It is one of the most cold-tolerant tortoise species, surviving harsh winters by brumating underground. It is popular in the pet trade due to its small size and hardy nature.

name: Ball Python
habitat: Grasslands and savannas of western and central Africa
funFact: Ball pythons curl into a tight ball with their head protected in the center when frightened, hence their name.
description: The ball python is a non-venomous constrictor native to the grasslands of western and central Africa. It is the most popular pet snake in the world due to its docile temperament and manageable size. It has hundreds of color morphs bred in captivity.

name: Cat-Eyed Snake
habitat: Tropical rainforests and cloud forests of Central and South America
funFact: Cat-eyed snakes have vertical pupils like cats, giving them excellent night vision for hunting in the dark rainforest.
description: The cat-eyed snake is a small, rear-fanged snake found in the tropical rainforests of Central and South America. It has distinctive vertical pupils and is primarily nocturnal. It feeds on frogs, lizards, and small mammals.

name: Arabian Chameleon
habitat: Arid shrublands and gardens of the Arabian Peninsula
funFact: Arabian chameleons are one of the few chameleon species adapted to live in hot, arid desert conditions.
description: The Arabian chameleon is a species of chameleon native to the Arabian Peninsula. It is adapted to arid conditions, unlike most chameleon species. It has a casque on its head and can change color for communication and thermoregulation.

name: Spotted Turtle
habitat: Shallow, slow-moving waters of eastern North America
funFact: Spotted turtles have yellow spots on their dark shells that become more numerous with age, like counting tree rings.
description: The spotted turtle is one of the smallest turtles in North America, found in shallow, slow-moving waters. It has a smooth, dark shell with distinctive yellow or orange spots. It is a long-lived species that can survive for over a century.

name: Banded Krait
habitat: Rice paddies, forests, and plains of South and Southeast Asia
funFact: Banded kraits are twice as venomous as cobras and often cannibalize other snakes, including other kraits.
description: The banded krait is a highly venomous elapid found in South and Southeast Asia. It has distinctive black and yellow bands and is primarily nocturnal. It feeds on other snakes, including venomous species, and is responsible for many snakebite deaths in Asia.

name: Golden Skink
habitat: Tropical forests and gardens of South and Southeast Asia
funFact: Golden skinks have a metallic, iridescent sheen that makes them look like they are coated in gold.
description: The golden skink is a small, fast-moving lizard found in tropical forests and gardens across South and Southeast Asia. It has a metallic, iridescent body that gives it a golden appearance. It is diurnal and feeds on insects and small invertebrates.

name: Broad-Snouted Caiman
habitat: Freshwater lakes, marshes, and slow-moving rivers of South America
funFact: Broad-snouted caimans build mounds of vegetation to incubate their eggs, using decomposition heat to warm them.
description: The broad-snouted caiman is a medium-sized crocodilian found in the freshwater habitats of South America. It has a broad, flat snout adapted for catching fish and invertebrates. It builds vegetation mounds to incubate its eggs.

name: Copperhead
habitat: Forests, rocky hillsides, and mixed woodlands of eastern North America
funFact: Copperheads account for the majority of venomous snakebites in the United States, though their venom is rarely fatal.
description: The copperhead is a venomous pit viper found across the eastern United States. It has a distinctive copper-colored head and hourglass-shaped crossbands. It is responsible for the most snakebite cases in North America, though fatalities are rare.

name: Radiated Tortoise
habitat: Dry spiny forests and grasslands of southern Madagascar
funFact: Radiated tortoises can live for over 100 years, with some individuals reportedly reaching 188 years of age.
description: The radiated tortoise is a critically endangered species endemic to Madagascar. It has a high-domed shell with striking yellow star-shaped patterns radiating from the center of each scute. It is threatened by habitat loss and poaching for food and the pet trade.

name: Blue Racer
habitat: Prairies, open woodlands, and farmlands of the central United States
funFact: Blue racers are one of the fastest snakes in North America, capable of speeds up to 10 mph.
description: The blue racer is a fast-moving, non-venomous colubrid found across the central United States and southern Ontario. It has a distinctive blue-grey dorsal color and a white or cream underside. It is diurnal and feeds on rodents, frogs, and other snakes.

name: Side-Blotched Lizard
habitat: Deserts, grasslands, and scrublands of western North America
funFact: Male side-blotched lizards use a rock-paper-scissors strategy with three throat colors to compete for mates.
description: The side-blotched lizard is a small lizard found in the deserts and grasslands of western North America. It is famous in evolutionary biology for its rock-paper-scissors mating strategy. Males have three throat colors that correspond to different mating tactics.

name: Nile Monitor
habitat: Rivers, lakes, and marshes throughout sub-Saharan Africa
funFact: Nile monitors are excellent swimmers and can hold their breath for up to an hour while submerged underwater.
description: The Nile monitor is a large, powerful lizard found throughout sub-Saharan Africa near water. It is semi-aquatic and feeds on fish, frogs, birds, eggs, and carrion. It has a forked tongue used for detecting prey in the water.

name: Canebrake Rattlesnake
habitat: Forests, canebrakes, and swamps of the southeastern United States
funFact: Canebrake rattlesnakes have a silent rattle compared to other rattlesnake species, often delivering strikes without warning.
description: The canebrake rattlesnake, a subspecies of the timber rattlesnake, is found in the forests and swamps of the southeastern United States. It has a distinctive pinkish-brown color with dark crossbands. It is a dangerous venomous pit viper.

name: Yellow-Footed Tortoise
habitat: Tropical rainforests of the Amazon Basin
funFact: Yellow-footed tortoises play a crucial role in seed dispersal in the Amazon, helping to regenerate the rainforest.
description: The yellow-footed tortoise is a medium-sized tortoise native to the Amazon Basin of South America. It has distinctive yellow or orange scales on its legs and head. It feeds primarily on fallen fruit and plays an important ecological role in seed dispersal.

name: Puff Adder
habitat: Savannas, grasslands, and scrublands of sub-Saharan Africa
funFact: Puff adders are responsible for more snakebite deaths in Africa than any other snake due to their excellent camouflage.
description: The puff adder is a venomous viper found throughout sub-Saharan Africa. It relies on its excellent camouflage and will not flee when approached, leading to many defensive strikes. It is an ambush predator that strikes with incredible speed.

name: Red-Eared Slider
habitat: Ponds, lakes, and rivers of the Mississippi Valley and Gulf Coast
funFact: Red-eared sliders are the most widely distributed turtle species in the world, considered one of the top 100 invasive species globally.
description: The red-eared slider is a semi-aquatic turtle native to the Mississippi Valley region of the United States. It is the most popular pet turtle in the world and has become a significant invasive species on every continent except Antarctica. It has a distinctive red stripe behind each eye.

name: Eastern Green Mamba
habitat: Coastal forests and woodlands of eastern and southern Africa
funFact: Eastern green mambas are arboreal and rarely descend to the ground, spending their lives in the forest canopy.
description: The eastern green mamba is a fast, highly venomous elapid found in the coastal forests of eastern and southern Africa. It is bright green, blending perfectly with the forest canopy. Unlike the black mamba, it is arboreal and rarely comes to the ground.

name: Cape Dwarf Chameleon
habitat: Shrublands, gardens, and fynbos of the Western Cape, South Africa
funFact: Cape dwarf chameleons have independently moving eyes that can rotate 180 degrees, giving them a 360-degree field of vision.
description: The Cape dwarf chameleon is a small chameleon endemic to the Western Cape of South Africa. It has independently rotating eyes, a prehensile tail, and a long, sticky tongue for catching insects. It can change color for communication and thermoregulation.

name: Chinese Alligator
habitat: Freshwater rivers, lakes, and wetlands of eastern China
funFact: Chinese alligators are the most endangered crocodilian species, with fewer than 150 individuals remaining in the wild.
description: The Chinese alligator is a critically endangered species, one of only two alligator species in the world. Found in eastern China, it is smaller than the American alligator and has bony plates on its eyelids. Wild populations are critically low.

name: Snouted Cobra
habitat: Savannas, grasslands, and coastal bush of southern Africa
funFact: Snouted cobras can spit venom accurately up to 2 meters, aiming for the eyes of perceived threats.
description: The snouted cobra is a large, highly venomous snake found across southern Africa. It has a distinctive upturned snout and can spit venom accurately. It is found in a wide variety of habitats and feeds on rodents, birds, and other snakes.

name: Common Wall Lizard
habitat: Stone walls, rocky outcrops, and urban areas of Europe
funFact: Common wall lizards have been introduced to North America from Europe and are now thriving in cities like Toronto and Vancouver.
description: The common wall lizard is a small, agile lizard found across Europe and introduced to North America. It is commonly seen basking on stone walls and buildings. It feeds on insects, spiders, and small invertebrates.

name: Brown Tree Snake
habitat: Forests, shrublands, and human structures in Australia, Papua New Guinea, and Guam
funFact: The brown tree snake has driven at least 10 bird species to extinction on Guam after accidentally introduced there.
description: The brown tree snake is an arboreal, rear-fanged snake native to Australia and New Guinea. It has become one of the world's most destructive invasive species on Guam, where it has eliminated most of the island's native bird species. It is nocturnal and feeds on birds, lizards, and mammals.

name: Angulate Tortoise
habitat: Fynbos and karoo shrublands of South Africa and Namibia
funFact: Angulate tortoises are the most southerly distributed tortoise species in Africa, found even in the cool, wet Western Cape.
description: The angulate tortoise is a small tortoise found in the fynbos and karoo shrublands of southern Africa. It has a distinctive upturned front margin to its shell. It is well adapted to the Mediterranean climate of the Western Cape region.

name: Savannah Monitor
habitat: Savannas, woodlands, and grasslands of sub-Saharan Africa
funFact: Savannah monitors can slow their metabolism so much that they can survive on as few as three large meals per year.
description: The savannah monitor is a medium-sized monitor lizard found across sub-Saharan Africa. It is a ground-dwelling species that digs burrows for shelter. It feeds on insects, small mammals, and reptiles, and is popular in the exotic pet trade.

name: White-Lipped Pit Viper
habitat: Tropical rainforests and bamboo groves of Southeast Asia
funFact: White-lipped pit vipers have heat-sensing pits between their eyes and nostrils that detect warm-blooded prey in complete darkness.
description: The white-lipped pit viper is a venomous snake found in the tropical rainforests of Southeast Asia. It has a distinctive white or yellow line along its upper lip and is primarily arboreal. It is a nocturnal ambush predator that feeds on rodents and birds.

name: Alabama Red-Bellied Cooter
habitat: Rivers, lakes, and ponds of Alabama and Georgia
funFact: Alabama red-bellied cooters can bask for hours, using the sun to synthesize vitamin D3 for shell health.
description: The Alabama red-bellied cooter is an endangered freshwater turtle endemic to Alabama and Georgia. It has a dark shell with a distinctive red or orange plastron. It is found in rivers, lakes, and ponds with abundant aquatic vegetation.

name: Amazon Tree Boa
habitat: Tropical rainforests of the Amazon Basin, arboreal
funFact: Amazon tree boas are incredibly variable in color and pattern, with no two individuals looking exactly alike.
description: The Amazon tree boa is a small, arboreal constrictor found throughout the Amazon rainforest. It is nocturnal and feeds on birds and small mammals. It has an extremely variable color pattern, ranging from yellow to red to brown.

name: California Kingsnake
habitat: Deserts, grasslands, forests, and suburban areas of the western United States
funFact: California kingsnakes are immune to rattlesnake venom and regularly prey upon rattlesnakes in the wild.
description: The California kingsnake is a popular, non-venomous constrictor found across the western United States. It has a banded pattern of brown and white or yellow. It is an opportunistic feeder that readily eats rattlesnakes, making it beneficial to humans.

name: Clouded Monitor
habitat: Tropical rainforests of Southeast Asia
funFact: Clouded monitors are arboreal and have sharp claws that allow them to climb vertical tree trunks with ease.
description: The clouded monitor is a medium-sized monitor lizard found in the tropical rainforests of Southeast Asia. It is arboreal and has a long, slender body adapted for climbing. It feeds on insects, small mammals, and birds.

name: Brazilian Rainbow Boa
habitat: Tropical rainforests of the Amazon and Orinoco Basins
funFact: Brazilian rainbow boas have iridescent scales that create a holographic rainbow effect when exposed to light.
description: The Brazilian rainbow boa is a medium-sized, non-venomous constrictor found in the rainforests of South America. Its name comes from the stunning iridescent sheen of its scales. It is primarily terrestrial and feeds on rodents, birds, and bats.

name: Northern Cuirassated Lizard
habitat: Rocky hillsides and scrublands of Mexico
funFact: Northern cuirassated lizards have bony armor plates called osteoderms that provide protection from predators.
description: The northern cuirassated lizard is a small lizard found in the rocky hillsides of Mexico. It has distinctive bony armor plates called osteoderms covering its body. It is diurnal and feeds on insects and small invertebrates.

name: Desert Iguana
habitat: Sonoran and Mojave Deserts of the southwestern United States
funFact: Desert iguanas can tolerate body temperatures up to 120°F, making them one of the most heat-tolerant lizards.
description: The desert iguana is a medium-sized lizard found in the deserts of the southwestern United States and northwestern Mexico. It is one of the most heat-tolerant lizards, active at temperatures that force other reptiles to seek shade. It feeds primarily on leaves and flowers.

name: False Water Cobra
habitat: Wetlands, marshes, and riverine forests of South America
funFact: False water cobras flatten their necks like true cobras when threatened, despite being only mildly venomous.
description: The false water cobra is a large, semi-aquatic colubrid found in the wetlands of South America. It displays a cobra-like hood when threatened, despite being only mildly venomous. It is an excellent swimmer and feeds on fish, frogs, and small mammals.

name: Common Garter Snake
habitat: Gardens, woodlands, and meadows across North America
funFact: Garter snakes are mildly venomous but harmless to humans, making them one of the most common backyard snakes.
description: The common garter snake is one of the most widespread snakes in North America, found in gardens, meadows, and woodlands. It has distinctive longitudinal stripes. Despite being mildly venomous, it is harmless to humans and beneficial as pest control.

name: Shingleback Skink
habitat: Woodlands, grasslands, and heathlands of southern Australia
funFact: Shingleback skinks mate for life and reunite with the same partner every breeding season.
description: The shingleback skink is a large, slow-moving lizard found in the woodlands and grasslands of southern Australia. It has rough, pinecone-like scales and a short, fat tail that resembles its head, confusing predators. It is one of the few reptile species that mate for life.

name: Thorny Devil
habitat: Arid spinifex grasslands and deserts of central Australia
funFact: Thorny devils have micro-channels in their skin that funnel water from any body part directly to their mouths.
description: The thorny devil is a small, spiny lizard native to the arid deserts of central Australia. Its entire body is covered in conical spines that provide defense against predators. Its skin has microscopic channels that collect water and transport it to its mouth.

name: Mozambique Spitting Cobra
habitat: Savannas, woodlands, and coastal forests of eastern and southern Africa
funFact: Mozambique spitting cobras can spit venom accurately up to 3 meters, targeting the eyes of threats.
description: The Mozambique spitting cobra is a highly venomous elapid found across eastern and southern Africa. It is one of the most dangerous snakes in the region, responsible for many snakebite cases. It can spit venom accurately into the eyes of perceived threats.
